title: NEB Class 11 English — Language Development — 2024
subject: english
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A generation ago a student who wanted to learn a trade had to find a master and serve an apprenticeship. Today the same skill is often learned from a screen: a video plays, the learner pauses, repeats the step, and fails privately until the hand remembers. The change looks like a small matter of convenience, but it shifts who bears the cost of learning. An apprentice's mistakes cost the master money and patience; a learner's mistakes cost only time. That protection is what makes the new learning so forgiving — and also what tempts a learner to stop before the difficult part, because nothing forces the hand to keep going except the learner's own intention.

(a) How did a student learn a trade a generation ago? (b) What does the writer mean by 'fails privately'? (c) According to the passage, what is both the advantage and the danger of learning from a screen? (d) Find a word from the passage that means 'the state of being protected from the consequences of error'.
questions.solution:
(a) A generation ago the student had to find a master and serve an apprenticeship, learning the skill by working under that master.

(b) It means the learner's mistakes are made where no one is watching or paying for them — the learner can repeat a step and fail without embarrassment, expense or a master's impatience.

(c) The advantage is that mistakes cost only time, so learning is forgiving and private; the danger is that nothing external forces the learner to continue, so a learner may stop before the difficult part unless they have their own strong intention.

(d) 'protection' — the passage says that protection (from the cost of mistakes) is what makes screen-based learning forgiving.
questions.knowledgeNote: Inference questions ask what the writer implies, not what the words literally say: 'fails privately' is explained by the contrast with an apprentice, whose mistakes cost the master.

questions.question: Write a paragraph of about 100 words, in your own words, explaining the main idea of the passage in the first question. Do not copy long phrases from the passage.
questions.solution: The passage contrasts two ways of learning a practical skill. In the past an apprentice learned from a master, and every mistake had a price — money, patience and reputation. Now the same skill can be learned from recorded lessons, where mistakes cost only time, so learning becomes private, repeatable and forgiving. The writer argues that this is not merely convenient: it changes what drives the learner. Because no master insists, the learner must supply the discipline himself; the freedom that protects a beginner can also let them quit exactly where the work becomes hard.
questions.knowledgeNote: A summary of a passage keeps the writer's argument and its contrast, stays within the word limit, and rewrites the wording rather than lifting sentences.
